jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Project Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Projects are initiated by internal product teams (CDN, Cloud, Edge AI, DDoS) or by Technical Support on behalf of external customers. At this level, the PM owns more than Jira tracking: the quality of the plan, realistic timelines, a sound budget estimate, risk management, and coordination of several parallel work streams - architects, procurement, logistics, data centre engineers, and operations teams.
We expect you to take on technically and organisationally complex projects - a large deployment at a new site, or a multi-vendor integration, and deliver them with minimal involvement from your manager, while proactively communicating status and risks.

Projects you will run:

  • PoP build-outs and colocation - new sites, expansion of existing ones, racks and cage space in third-party data centres.
  • Server and network hardware deployments for internal product demand and for external customers (dedicated hardware, managed connectivity).
  • Capacity expansion, hardware refresh, and decommissioning.
  • Connectivity and interconnection procurement - IP transit, cross-connects, dark fibre, wavelengths, leased lines, in coordination with the Procurement team.
  • Migrations and relocations of physical equipment between sites.

What You’ll Do

End-to-end project ownership

  • Setting the project up in Jira (GI master ticket), breaking it down into tasks, and building a realistic schedule that accounts for dependencies.
  • Identifying the critical path and key risks at kick-off - without waiting for your manager to do it.
  • Orchestrating linked tasks across counterpart teams' Jira projects: IDS (architecture), PRO (procurement), DCI (on-site installation), HDWR (repair and replacement). Knowing where the work physically lives, and reporting on the active linked tickets, not just the master ticket.
  • Making operational decisions inside the project yourself. Escalating only what sits outside your authority: budget, priorities between projects, conflicts with other departments - and bringing a recommendation when you do.

Budget estimation and approvals

  • Owning the project budget at the Initiation stage: reviewing the cost estimate built on the architect's specification - breakdown by NRC / MRC and by component (colocation, leased lines, hardware, small parts) - and benchmarking it against comparable past projects and reference cost tables.
  • Driving the project through the approval chain, tracking approval turnaround, and handling objections.
  • Reconciling budget plan versus actuals at project closure.

Technical design and architecture

  • Briefing the Infrastructure Architects team (RFS / HLD / SDD) and contributing substantively to discussions on BoM, rack layout, power, and network.
  • The architect owns the specification - what is bought and where it is shipped. The PM controls it against the project's scope, timeline, and budget, and gets it approved.
  • Being able to tell a realistic technical plan from an unrealistic one, and challenging the design where it doesn't fit the project's constraints.

Procurement

  • Raising requests to the Procurement team based on the architect's specification, setting the deadline and project context, and tracking execution. Vendor negotiations are run by Procurement.
  • Monitoring request and PO statuses, and escalating early when timelines are at risk.

Logistics and delivery to site

  • Raising delivery requests to the Logistics team based on the architect's specification (what goes where), setting deadlines, and tracking execution. Shipping, customs, warehousing, and delivery to the data centre are run by the Logistics team.
  • Tracking ETAs and escalating early when delivery is at risk of slipping.

On-site installation

  • Briefing the DCIM team on equipment installation: agreeing installation windows, tracking timelines and quality of execution.
  • Handling discrepancies found at acceptance: missing equipment, equipment routed to stock, equipment routed to repair.

Hand-over to operations

  • Running the hand-over to the Server Operations and Network Operations teams. These teams sit outside the Infrastructure Department, so the hand-over requires explicit agreements on content, quality, and timing: documentation, configurations, monitoring on-boarding.
  • Organising and confirming acceptance testing, formally closing the project (sign-off), and capturing lessons learned.

Risk and stakeholder management

  • Identifying risks proactively, before they become problems, and proposing options rather than only reporting the issue.
  • Communicating regularly and substantively with stakeholders at different levels: product teams, vendors, operations teams, leadership.
  • Agreeing responsibility boundaries (RACI) with customers and partners on customer-facing and partner projects.
  • Managing scope changes: assessing impact on timeline and budget, getting agreement, recording it in Jira.

Flow and metrics (Kanban)

  • The team operates as a Kanban system: no sprints, with WIP limits and flow metrics. Jira statuses are the source of truth for all reporting, so status hygiene is part of the job rather than a nice-to-have: tickets move when work actually starts and finishes, not at the end of the week and not retroactively.
  • Understanding the difference between Customer Lead Time (what the requester experiences) and System Lead Time (what the team controls), working to the target P85 for your components, and acting on your own Aging WIP before your manager has to point it out.

Process improvement

  • Driving improvements to processes and templates inside IPM: RACI, readiness checklists, documentation standards, status entry and exit criteria — spotting what slows projects down and proposing concrete fixes.

What We're Looking For:

  • Minimum 3 years in project management in infrastructure, data centres, telecom, or IT operations, including projects with multiple counterpart teams or vendors. Running complex projects without step-by-step support is a hard requirement.
  • Solid understanding of server and network hardware and how a data centre works: racks, PDUs, power and cooling, basic network topology (switches, cross-connects, IP addressing) - at a level sufficient for a substantive conversation with architects and engineers, not just to recognise the terminology.
  • Experience with Jira (or an equivalent tracker) at project-administration level: linking tasks across projects, working with workflows and fields, not only changing statuses.
  • A high degree of personal ownership and autonomy: you keep your projects under control, surface risks yourself, and keep the team informed on substance without being asked.
  • Ability to work with ambiguity and to run several projects and workstreams in parallel.
  • English at B2 or above - enough for correspondence and negotiation with international partners and vendors. Documentation is written in English.
  • Strong communication skills: able to convey complex technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with flow-based management (Kanban) and with Lead Time, Throughput, and WIP metrics.
  • Experience in customer-facing or multi-partner projects with a formal RACI.
  • Experience with budget estimation for infrastructure projects (NRC / MRC, colocation, leased lines).
  • Project management certification (PMP, Kanban Management Professional, or similar).
  • Experience working in a distributed international team.

Benefits

At Gcore, we want you to do your best work and enjoy the journey. Our benefits are designed to support your growth, well-being, and life beyond work:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Flexible working hours and hybrid or remote options, depending on your role
  • Work from anywhere in the world for up to 45 days per year
  • Private medical insurance for you and your family*
  • Extra paid vacation and sick leave days*
  • Support for life’s important moments and celebrations
  • Language courses to help you connect and grow
  • Modern, welcoming offices with snacks, drinks, and entertainment*
  • Team sports and social activities*

*Benefits may vary depending on your location.

Equal Opportunity Employer

We provide equal opportunity to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, disability, or any other legally protected characteristics.

The world’s digital experiences run on something invisible: the infrastructure and software that keep them fast, reliable, and secure. At Gcore, you’ll help design and deliver that foundation for an AI-driven world.

We’re a global provider of infrastructure and software solutions for AI, cloud, network, and security, powering everything from real-time communication and streaming to enterprise AI and secure web applications. With 210+ edge locations, 50+ cloud regions, and thousands of GPUs, your work here can reach users and businesses across the globe.

You’ll collaborate with leading technology partners such as Intel, NVIDIA, Dell, and Equinix, and work on platforms that power digital products used around the world. Our vision is simple: to connect the world to AI, anywhere, anytime.

Want to work on technology that goes beyond a single product or industry? Join a global team of 550+ professionals building infrastructure and software that supports the entire digital ecosystem.

We are currently looking for a SeniorInfrastructure Project Manager, who will independently run projects that deploy and change Gcore infrastructure - from intake through hand-over to operations and formal closure.
This is not a role for learning the basics: we expect someone who already runs complex projects end-to-end, makes operational decisions without day-to-day oversight, and resolves priority and resource conflicts on their own.

jobs.jd_full:
About Aegis Ventures

Aegis Ventures is a next-generation startup studio that partners with entrepreneurs and industry leaders to originate, launch, and scale transformative companies, with a focus on artificial intelligence. The Aegis platform brings together market-shaping ideas, permanent growth capital, and ambitious individuals who are driven to solve major societal problems. Our companies use technology to transform healthcare by dramatically improving quality, access, and cost. Aegis creates new companies with substantial input from our Digital Consortium of a dozen leading health systems and other ecosystem partners. We have launched 6 innovative companies to date and are just getting started.

About Caregentic

Caregentic builds AI infrastructure for continuous care operations. Our condition-agnostic platform runs the operating layer between clinical visits: it guides patients through care journeys, turns their conversations into structured clinical data written back into the EHR, and escalates the signals care teams need to act on. We work alongside Epic, Cerner, and Athena, not in place of them, and partner with health systems including Northwell Health and Endeavor Health. We are AI-native and human-first in how we build: our engineers work with AI coding agents every day, and people stay accountable for every decision that touches a patient.

About the Job

As a Senior Product Manager at Caregentic, you will own our product roadmap and turn priorities into clear, actionable work for engineering. You will build deep product knowledge, understand customer and user needs, write detailed requirements, and validate that delivered features meet expectations.

This is a senior individual contributor role with meaningful ownership of prioritization and delivery. Working with leadership, you will translate company goals into a practical roadmap and make day-to-day scope and priority decisions within agreed objectives and engineering capacity.

This role reports to the COO and works closely with the CEO and CTO. Product vision and long-range strategy sit with the CEO, CTO and COO. You own the rolling roadmap, the backlog, and the requirements that turn priorities into shipped work.

What You’ll Do:

  • Use AI, own the output. Use Claude and similar tools to draft, analyze, and pressure-test requirements, explore user flows, and build quick prototypes. Then personally review every epic for clarity, completeness, and acceptance criteria before it reaches engineering.
  • Own the roadmap and backlog both as standalone documents and as part of code repo in GitHub. Maintain near-term delivery priorities and longer-term direction, gather input, and communicate decisions, tradeoffs, and what is outside the current scope.
  • Write requirements for people and agents. Personally create and maintain product requirements (PRDs) in our GitHub repository, linked to Jira epics, covering frontend and backend behavior, user flows, and acceptance criteria, so engineers and the AI coding agents they work with share the same context. When scope changes mid-sprint, update the PRD first and make sure the engineering plan and tickets follow.
  • Keep delivery moving. Partner with engineering on backlog refinement and sprint planning, contribute actively to relevant stand-ups, and respond promptly to product questions throughout development.
  • Validate delivered work. Review functionality against requirements, identify gaps and bugs, and follow through with engineering on fixes and product acceptance before release.
  • Bring customer evidence into decisions. Speak with clients and users, synthesize feedback from commercial and delivery teams, and use relevant market and competitive insight to shape priorities.
  • Build the platform, not one-offs. Turn client requests into reusable, condition-agnostic capabilities and care journey templates. Balance customer value, business goals, risk, and effort, push back on hard-coded, client-specific logic, and escalate material exceptions to leadership.
  • Define clear workflows. Explain intended behavior in plain language and detail; create lightweight wireframes or prototypes where helpful; and collaborate with available design and engineering partners on usability.
  • Maintain product knowledge and documentation as standalone documents and as Github code repo artifacts. Keep requirements, decisions, and feature changes current. Help colleagues understand capabilities and coordinate documentation and release updates.
  • Translate constraints and learn from releases. Work with clinical, security, and compliance experts on product requirements. Define success measures and use adoption and user feedback to improve what ships.
  • Keep demos accurate. Own the content of our demo library (which care journeys we show and what each demo proves), working with engineering on the build.
  • Keep requirements traceable. Maintain a clear line from each requirement to its acceptance criteria, tests, and release, and put security and compliance checkpoints (such as SOC 2, TCPA, and future FDA work) on the roadmap so they never show up as surprises.

What You’ll Need:

  • 5+ years in software product management, or equivalent experience demonstrating independent ownership of roadmap priorities and delivery.
  • Strong hands-on requirements writing, including clear product specifications, acceptance criteria, and practical experience managing work in Jira or a comparable tool.
  • Proven experience leveraging AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, or specialized product extensions) to drive efficiency across product development workflows, from early-stage ideation and feature scoping to lightweight prototyping and specification writing.
  • A track record of working closely with engineers to resolve ambiguity, make scope decisions, validate delivered functionality, and follow work through to completion.
  • Technical fluency to discuss frontend and backend behavior, integrations, data flows, and feasibility with engineering. Architecture and implementation decisions remain with engineering.
  • Experience gathering customer feedback and making prioritization decisions with incomplete information, including explaining decisions to both executives and engineers.
  • Experience with healthcare workflows and the ability to translate clinical, privacy, security, and compliance needs into product requirements with appropriate experts.
  • Practical UX judgment, clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to organize your own work in an early-stage company with limited resources.
  • Experience working in an early-stage startup or similarly small, resource-constrained software team, with direct responsibility for both roadmap priorities and hands-on product delivery.
  • Comfort working cross-functionally with engineering, clinical and customer partners.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to earn trust quickly.
  • A builder’s mindset: you’d rather prototype and test an idea than debate it.
  • Mission alignment: a real drive to use technology to improve patient care.

Bonus Points For:

  • B2B software for hospitals or health systems, including EHR integrations such as Epic.
  • Patient engagement, care management, workflow automation, or AI-enabled products.
  • Hands-on experience using AI assistants and advanced LLM skills (such as custom Claude projects or prompt engineering for product specs) to streamline day-to-day product management tasks.
  • Working with Github repos and working with product management repo artifacts.
  • Basic experience in using and running database queries to support analytics needs of the product.
  • Lightweight prototyping in Figma or with AI tools, and collaboration with product designers.
  • Experience with Healthcare integration standards such as HL7 and FHIR.
  • Experience taking a product through Series A to growth stage.

What You’ll Bring to the Table:

  • Engineering partnership: Ability to give engineering clear requirements and timely answers, and to set clear decision rights and a practical working rhythm with the team.
  • Roadmap ownership: Experience building and maintaining a shared, prioritized roadmap, and explaining the priorities and the reasons behind them so the team understands them.
  • Delivery discipline: A consistent approach to product acceptance and change communication, so that delivered features meet agreed acceptance criteria.
  • Customer-informed judgment: Comfort meeting customers and stakeholders, learning user workflows quickly, and using customer evidence to guide decisions.
  • A habit of continuous improvement: Learning from adoption and feedback after release, then refining the roadmap and process to match.
  • Pragmatic execution: Ability to take a priority improvement through the full delivery cycle at a pace that fits the scope of the work and the release cadence.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Comprehensive healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision).
  • Flexible PTO with 20 vacation days and 5 sick days per year.
  • 401(k) retirement plan.
  • Fully remote work environment.
  • Top-tier development equipment.
  • The chance to make a meaningful impact on healthcare delivery.

Salary Range:

  • We offer a competitive compensation package, including:
    • $140,000 - $165,000 base salary, depending on experience and alignment with role expectations.
    • Performance-based bonus.
    • Equity participation in the company.

Why Caregentic?

Healthcare teams shouldn’t have to wrestle with fragmented systems, duplicate data entry, or workflows that break when they need them most. Our unified platform uses AI to connect patient data, clinical protocols, and care coordination — surfacing insights and streamlining processes to create seamless experiences that improve outcomes while reducing administrative burden.

We believe the future of healthcare technology isn’t about replacing human judgment but amplifying it with intelligent automation. Every line of code we write and every model we deploy has one goal: helping healthcare professionals provide better care, more efficiently.

This is a rare opportunity to work on cutting-edge technology that directly impacts patient care, alongside a team that moves fast, learns from real clinical feedback, and builds with purpose. We’re backed by top-tier health systems like Northwell Health, building hand-in-hand with clinicians and shipping into live care settings from day one.

Position Summary

RethinkFirst is seeking a detail-oriented and motivated Associate Product Manager to support the continued development and enhancement of BillAI, our revenue cycle management (RCM) platform.

This position will work closely with the Senior Product Manager, engineering, QA, customer support, billing operations, and other internal stakeholders to manage product requirements, coordinate development activities, and support successful feature releases.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, comfortable working with technical and non-technical teams, and interested in developing a career in product management.

This role will focus on product execution, operational support, and assisting the Senior Product Manager with strategic initiatives, roadmap planning, and complex product decisions. As the individual develops product knowledge and experience, they will take increasing ownership of assigned features and enhancements.

Key Responsibilities

1. Product Requirements & Documentation

  • Assist the Senior Product Manager in gathering, documenting, and refining product requirements.

  • Create and maintain user stories, acceptance criteria, and functional requirements for development.

  • Work with stakeholders to clarify business needs, identify workflow challenges, and define expected functionality.

  • Maintain accurate product documentation, workflows, and feature specifications.

  • Ensure development tickets contain sufficient information for engineering and QA teams.

2. Product Backlog & Sprint Support

  • Assist with maintaining, organizing, and refining the product backlog.

  • Prepare user stories and requirements for sprint planning and backlog refinement sessions.

  • Track the progress of assigned development initiatives and identify potential blockers.

  • Coordinate with engineering and QA to clarify requirements throughout development.

  • Verify that completed work aligns with documented requirements and acceptance criteria.

  • Support the Senior Product Manager in monitoring sprint commitments and release timelines.

3. Stakeholder Coordination

  • Serve as a point of contact for internal stakeholders submitting product enhancement requests or reporting workflow gaps.

  • Gather additional information needed to evaluate requests and understand business impact.

  • Track stakeholder requests and provide regular updates on their status.

  • Coordinate meetings to review requirements, proposed solutions, and completed functionality.

  • Document meeting outcomes, action items, and follow-up activities.

  • Maintain visibility into product initiatives, customer-impacting issues, and development progress.

4. Product Testing & Release Support

  • Participate in reviewing completed functionality before release.

  • Assist with user acceptance testing (UAT) to verify that features meet business requirements.

  • Coordinate and conduct product demonstrations with internal stakeholders.

  • Prepare release notes and assist with communicating upcoming product changes.

  • Support post-release follow-up to identify issues or opportunities for improvement.

  • Work with QA and engineering to ensure reported defects are clearly documented and reproducible.

5. Customer Support & Product Operations

  • Partner with customer support and billing operations to understand recurring customer challenges.

  • Investigate reported product issues and help determine whether they are defects, training opportunities, or enhancement requests.

  • Document common product workflows and frequently asked questions.

  • Assist in creating internal training materials and product demonstrations.

  • Identify opportunities to improve existing workflows, reduce manual processes, and enhance the user experience.

6 . Product Ownership & Continuous Improvement

  • Take ownership of assigned product enhancements, including requirements gathering, stakeholder communication, development coordination, and release validation, with guidance from the Senior Product Manager.

  • Develop an understanding of healthcare revenue cycle management, including claims processing, payment posting, denials, and reporting.

  • Become familiar with healthcare EDI transactions, including 837 claims, 835 remittances, and claim acknowledgments.

  • Develop a strong understanding of the BillAI platform’s functionality, configurations, and integration workflows.

  • Identify opportunities to improve product processes, documentation, and stakeholder communication.

  • Gradually assume responsibility for independently managing smaller product features and enhancements.

  • Collaborate with the Senior Product Manager to evaluate potential solutions and recommend improvements based on customer needs and business impact.

Required Qualifications

  • 1–3 years of experience in product management, business analysis, software implementation, project coordination, or a related role.

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to translate business needs into clear, actionable requirements.

  • Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.

  • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum software development methodologies.

  • Experience using product management or issue-tracking tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or similar platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with healthcare software or SaaS platforms.

  • Familiarity with healthcare revenue cycle management workflows.

  • Basic understanding of medical claims, insurance payments, denials, and adjustments.

  • Exposure to healthcare EDI transactions, including 837, 835, 999, and 277.

  • Experience writing user stories and acceptance criteria.

  • Experience supporting software testing or user acceptance testing.

  • Familiarity with behavioral health or ABA billing is a plus.

Success Measures

Success in this role will be measured by the individual’s ability to:

  • Maintain well-documented, organized, and actionable product requirements.

  • Improve the readiness of development tickets before sprint planning.

  • Ensure stakeholder requests are tracked, evaluated, and communicated effectively.

  • Support timely completion of product demonstrations and release activities.

  • Reduce the administrative and coordination workload of the Senior Product Manager.

  • Demonstrate increasing ownership of assigned product enhancements from requirements through release.

  • Develop sufficient product knowledge to independently manage smaller features and enhancements.

  • Build effective working relationships with engineering, QA, customer support, and billing operations.

  • Contribute to improvements in product workflows, stakeholder communication, and overall team efficiency.

jobs.jd_full:
ABOUT OUR COMPANY:

The crushing weight of debt is something that we believe holds people back from reaching their dreams and making a splash in the world. So in 2013, after seeing our friends and family struggle with student loans, we created Splash Financial.

Over the years, our mission has expanded to include helping people with other forms of debt - such as refinancing credit cards, which are at all time highs in the US. And we’ve been able to refinance $6+ Billion in loans through our network of Splash, powered credit union and bank partners who leverage our marketplace and automated loan processing technology. And we’ve raised over $135 million from investors like partners of DST Global, Citi Ventures, TruStage Ventures, Northwestern Mutual Future Ventures, Detroit Venture Partners, and more.

But at our core, we’re still that little company from Cleveland with a big dream: to make people more powerful than their debt and we’re just getting started..

ABOUT OUR WORKPLACE:

Splash is remote-first, and proud of it — though our collections team works in-person at our Arizona location.

We spend our days simplifying financial products and getting them into the hands of people who need them most. Right now, we’re focused on building financial technologies that fundamentally transform how the industry lends.

Although Splash has been around since 2013, we still operate like a startup — fast-paced, nimble, and full of heart. We’re good people who care deeply about doing meaningful work and we approach challenges with creativity, passion, and urgency.

And to hire the best, we provide the best: great health insurance, competitive salaries, and unique benefits like quarterly meet-ups and access to engagement tools that keep us connected — even from afar.

At Splash, everything we do is guided by our values:

Own It – We take full accountability and follow through on commitments.

Raise the Bar – We move fast, innovate faster, and push through barriers.

Say the Hard Thing – We speak up with honesty, respect, and a desire to solve problems and make things better.

Elevate Each Other – We win as a team by lifting each other up.

These values show up in how we work and how we connect — whether we’re collaborating on big projects or bonding over everyday moments. Yes, we even have Slack channels for #kids-and-pets and #food because we believe being human makes us better teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Splash Financial is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own the underwriting experience for our Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) product, one of the biggest growth opportunities for Splash. Most HELOCs still take weeks to close, with manual underwriting, slow appraisals, and paper-heavy closings. You’ll own the product strategy and roadmap for how a HELOC moves from submitted application to close: income and employment verification, property valuation, document review, conditions, and tools our underwriters and operations team use every day.  Your goal: make HELOCs faster, simpler, and more automated than anything else on the market.

This is a highly cross-functional and high impact role within a broader HELOC product team. You’ll sit at the center of engineering, design, credit, operations, compliance, and our lending partners, aligning them around clear priorities and shared outcomes. You’ll dig into operational and funnel data to find where loans stall, test your hypotheses, and turn what you learn into measurable gains time to fund, conversion, operational efficiency and borrower experience. As a senior member of the product team, you’ll also help raise the bar for how we build at Splash.

WHAT YOU’LL DO AT SPLASH:

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for HELOC underwriting, from submitted application through close, including income and employment verification, property valuation, document review, and condition clearing.  Own time-to-fund as a core metric. Map the end-to-end loan lifecycle, find where loans stall, and ship changes that reduce time from application to funding without adding risk.
  • Drive underwriting and operational efficiency by working closely with credit and operations to reduce manual touches, shorten condition-clearing cycles, and increase loans processed per underwriter. Treat internal teams as customers of the product, because a faster operation means a better borrower experience.
  • Lead the AI and automation roadmap for HELOC underwriting and operations. Identify where AI can classify and extract data from borrower documents, flag discrepancies, recommend or auto-clear conditions, and route only true exceptions to people.
  • Expand automated valuation coverage by partnering with credit and valuation vendors to increase AVM eligibility, improve hit rates, and reduce reliance on full appraisals.
  • Build a state-aware closing experience with compliance, title, and e-closing partners, maximizing digital and remote online closings where permitted.
  • Lead cross-functional teams across engineering, design, credit, operations, compliance, and marketing from discovery through launch, writing clear requirements and making the tradeoffs that keep delivery on track.
  • Partner with third-party vendors (such as valuation, title, document, and e-closing providers) to translate partner and regulatory requirements into scalable product solutions.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO SPLASH:

  • 6+ years of product management experience in consumer technology or fintech, with a proven track record of shipping impactful products and owning outcomes end to end.
  • A working knowledge of consumer lending underwriting, credit decisioning, income and employment verification, document review, and conditions, and how product decisions affect credit risk and compliance.
  • A true cross-functional team player: you build trust with engineering, design, operations, credit, compliance, and business partners, influence without authority, and bring people together around shared goals.
  • A data-driven approach to decisions, with hands-on experience in product analytics, funnel analysis, experimentation, and operational metrics (cycle time, touch time, throughput), plus the judgment to turn insights into improvements that move key metrics.
  • Experience improving operational workflows or building internal tools, ideally where you reduced manual work, cycle time, or cost-to-serve while improving the customer experience.
  • A builder’s view of AI: you’ve used AI and automation in products or workflows (such as document intelligence, decisioning, or process automation) and use AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor daily to speed up research, analysis, and documentation.

NICE TO HAVE:

  • Strongly preferred: Direct experience with HELOC, home equity, or mortgage products, especially underwriting or loan operations.
  • Familiarity with the HELOC underwriting lifecycle and LOS systems, such as AVMs and appraisals, title, income and employment verification, e-closing, and lien recording.
  • Experience in a regulated environment, working closely with compliance on requirements such as TILA, RESPA, ECOA, or HMDA.
  • Experience working with bank, credit union, or platform partners to deliver product changes.
  • SQL proficiency and experience with BI and product analytics tools (e.g., Snowflake, Sigma).

COMPENSATION:

The base salary range for this role is $145,000 to $185,000 annually, based on market data and internal compensation practices. This role may also be eligible for a bonus component tied to individual and company performance. Final compensation will be determined by factors such as location, experience, and skill level.

SPLASHERS ENJOY:

  • Fully remote work freedom (for most roles)
  • Competitive salary packages
  • Flexible PTO + 9 company holidays
  • Equity: Share in our start-up success
  • Comprehensive and affordable insurance benefits
  • Paid parental leave for both caregivers
  • Essential modern equipment to get the job done
  • Fully paid Claude subscription to supercharge your work
  • 401(k) for your future savings
  • Quarterly meet-ups: In person & virtual fun
  • Awesome Splash swag to flaunt your team spirit

Employment at Splash is based on individual merit. Opportunities are open to all, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, creed, age, handicap, national origin, ancestry, military status, veteran status, medical condition, marital status, sexual orientation, affectional preference, or other irrelevant factors. Splash is an equal opportunity employer.

JOB OFFER & RECRUITMENT SCAM NOTICE

At Splash Financial, we want candidates to feel confident and safe throughout the hiring process. Unfortunately, scammers sometimes pose as employers to trick job seekers into sharing personal information or money.

PLEASE BE AWARE:

  • Splash Financial will never ask for payment, banking details, or cryptocurrency as part of our hiring process.

  • We do not conduct interviews solely via text message or chat apps.

IF YOU RECEIVE A SUSPICIOUS MESSAGE:

  • Report the message to careers@splashfinancial.com
